notes: Flow branches: after the deputy-SG/secretary-general resolution (10-2-32/31), 10-2-10 branches on resolution_type DENY -> deny_case, else on case_state: CLOSED -> close_case, INVESTIGATING -> committee_memo/committee_dispatch/board_round2 -> notice. Modelled with separate per-branch tables (deny_case, close_case, notice) plus the shared committee/board-round-2 tables.

Preliminary resolution (10-2-06, round_no=1, stage SUBCOMMITTEE) and the final resolution (10-2-32 DEPUTY or 10-2-31 SECGEN, round_no=2) overwrite the same l2Resolution*/l2CaseState* fields in the mockup. Fixed by giving each round its own row in the resolution table; case_file keeps only the latest values for convenient reads.

Send-back loops at 10-2-04 (REVISE -> back to 10-2-03) and at 10-2-26/10-2-27 (send back -> back to 10-2-25, unsigning the prior signer) overwrite l2VerifyResult/l2VerifyNotes and the committee memo fields respectively in the mockup. Fixed with group_verify.round_no and committee_memo.round_no so every round is preserved; the send-back reason is also duplicated onto case_transition.note for a single chronological audit trail.

10-2-09 legal-admin-dispatch does not set l2ApprovalBranch; only 10-2-32 (when in_skipSecgen is checked) writes l2ApprovalBranch=DEPUTY. 10-2-31 (secretary-general path) never writes l2ApprovalBranch even though seed data shows SECGEN. Modelled case_file.approval_branch as nullable and populated by 10-2-32 only; a migration/back-fill rule (secgen path -> SECGEN) is left as an open question.
l2Signatures has about 34 named slots (LAW0038 ... appealNotifyAppellant), collapsed into one signature table keyed by (case_id or appeal_id, step_code) instead of one column per slot.

ECMIS102.openSignatureModal reports mode ("hand" or "cert") to the caller but the mockup never persists it into l2Signatures. Added signature.sign_method to close that gap; source pages do not populate it today.

The signer name is never stored in the mockup (only the signature image and, for cert mode, a certId not saved either). signature.signer_name and signature.cert_id are added as gap-fix columns and will be null for data migrated from the current mockup.

About 12 file-name arrays across steps (attachmentFileNames, l2SecretariatOpinionFile, l2Appeal*AttachmentFileNames, scannedDocFile) are unified into one attachment table. Files picked at 10-2-11 (in_noticeFile), 10-2-15 (in_denyMemoFile) and 10-2-22 (in_closeMemoFile) are shown in a preview only and never saved by the mockup; the attachment table can hold them once a real upload endpoint exists.

9 document number/date pairs (internal memo, dispatch, deny memo, close memo, committee memo, committee dispatch, notice, appeal board dispatch/reply, appeal notice) are unified into one document_number table with doc_type distinguishing them, instead of 9 separate column pairs.

Appeal (Flow 4) is modelled as its own appeal table (1:N from case_file) plus appeal_step (1:N from appeal), instead of writing l2Appeal* fields onto the same request row as the mockup does. This is a deliberate design decision: it lets one request have more than one appeal and keeps the appeal status_code independent from the base case status_code (which stays L2_CASE_CLOSED_DENY_ASSIGNED). signature/attachment/document_number gained a nullable appeal_id so appeal-step signatures, files and doc numbers can be linked to the appeal instead of the case.

No page in the mockup starts an appeal: entry status L2_PENDING_APPEAL_INTAKE is only ever set by seed data (no "start appeal" button exists on any DENY case screen). The DB still supports it (appeal.status_code can be set to L2_PENDING_APPEAL_INTAKE by an external process or a future button).

The appeal board result (l2AppealBoardResolutionType at appeal-11, which can reverse the original DENY) is never written back onto the original request/resolution in the mockup. appeal_step.result_code stores it, but case_file.l2_resolution_type_code is left untouched; a real system likely needs an explicit reconciliation step, left as an open question.

L2_BOARD_RESOLVED_ROUND2, L2_PENDING_APPEAL_INTAKE and L2_APPEAL_BOARD_RESOLVED are statuses no page writes (set externally by Activity 7 or missing UI); they are still included in the status lookup because seed data and ROUTES reference them.

l2BoardApprovalRef/l2BoardApprovalDate (shown read-only at 10-2-11) and l2RedactionNotes/l2RedactionDone exist only in seed data with no writer page in the mockup; kept as nullable case_file columns and flagged as gaps rather than dropped, since the brief asks to persist everything that passes through the flow including known gaps.

issueDocNo()/issueInternalDocNo() and signedAt store Thai-formatted display strings (e.g. "3 กันยายน 2569", "3 กันยายน 2569(BE) เวลา HH:mm น.") rather than ISO values. document_number.doc_date and signature.signed_at are typed date/timestamptz per the brief convention; a conversion step is required when migrating the mockup seed data.

Seed data has duplicate ids (คำร้อง-100033/2569, 100034, 100035, 100038 each appear twice, once in the appeal set and once in the committee/round-2 set); case_file.case_no is declared unique, so seed migration must de-duplicate or disambiguate these before loading.

The 01-work-inbox.html mock rows use a legacy, non-L2_ status vocabulary (FORWARDED_DIVISION, PENDING_OPINION, ...) that does not match the STEPS/ROUTES statusCode values used everywhere else; these are treated as a display-only legacy source and are not modelled as DB rows.
